span.term: When evidence is weak the accumulator drifts only slowly away from the decision boundary, so it takes longer to establish which side it is on, which is why difficult decisions are slow.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: FOF acts downstream of accumulation, categorizing the accumulator's value into a choice, which is why its activity is required near the go cue rather than throughout the stimulus.

span.label: RETRACTED (NEITHER ENDPOINT IS IN THE SPAN, AND THE RELATION IS HEDGED THREE TIMES) · frontal orienting fields —same-as→ frontal eye fields
span.note: RETRACTED: NEITHER ENDPOINT IS IN THE SPAN, AND THE RELATION IS HEDGED THREE TIMES. The edge is `frontal orienting fields --same-as--> frontal eye fields`. The span: 'these HAD BEEN SUGGESTED AS ANALOGOUS OR PERHAPS EVEN HOMOLOGOUS to the two key primate regions PPC and FEF, respectively.' The span names `PPC` and `FEF`; it does not contain `frontal orienting fields` or `frontal eye fields` as words at all - the endpoints were supplied from the tagger's vocabulary, THE SAME FAULT AS Gelbard-Sagiv2008's absent `reactivation`. This edge PREDATES the Q-267 gate check and could not be written today. On top of that: `suggested as`, `analogous`, and `perhaps even` are three hedges in eleven words, and `respectively` means the sentence maps TWO pairs at once, so even the intended relation is half of a two-way mapping. — strength of the relation: 0.7
